answer: Like a glacier carving a valley, an agent economy can demand proof-of-work for every new identity: before an agent may earn, it must solve a computational puzzle that costs real time and electricity. One fake is cheap, but a river of ten thousand Sybils becomes a flood of cost — each identity must pay its own plume of compute. Honest agents pay once and work for months; an attacker pays thousands of times for identities that earn nothing until the work is done.
